name: NVR, Inc.
moat_justification: The lot-option (LPA) model is a structural capital advantage proven through full housing cycles: NVR controls finished lots via fixed-price purchase agreements instead of owning/developing land, so invested capital stays minimal, returns on capital run far above land-owning peers (ROE above 30% through the cycle; FY2025 ROE ~34.7% per secondary reporting of the 10-K), and downturn risk is capped at forfeited deposits (~10% of lot value). Mortgage banking capture of 85% in Q2 2026 adds an attached, high-return ancillary. Against: the model is being copied by larger peers moving asset-light, buyers have no switching costs and pricing power is currently negative (Q2 2026 homebuilding gross margin 19.2% vs 21.5% a year earlier, order ASP -5%), lot supply depends on third-party developers, and the footprint is concentrated in 16 states + DC on the East Coast. fundamentals.json roic_proxy is null for every year because NVR files no operating-income tag, so the returns evidence is stated in words from the filings/earnings releases rather than quoted from that series.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
BUYBACK_TAILWIND: share count shrinking 4.4%/yr — already credited via the growth adjustment

DEBT_TAGS_BLANK: no debt tag reports for the latest fiscal year — net debt is UNKNOWN (not zero); no leverage verdict is possible from the engine, state the balance sheet from the filing in analysis.md

CASH_INCLUDES_RESTRICTED: the only cash tag filed for the latest fiscal year is the combined cash + restricted-cash total and no restricted-cash tag separates it — net debt is UNDERSTATED by the restricted amount (escrow / collateral / regulatory); check the balance sheet before trusting HIGH_NET_DEBT's absence
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 5.2x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
TIER_BAND: bear-case tier D (6.6%) vs bull-case tier C (11.2%) — the verdict spans tiers; size any position to the bear end
one_liner: Best-in-class asset-light homebuilder, moat 7/10 — but at $5,919.82 the weighted IRR is only 8.7% (weighted IV@15% $2,901); it clears the 15% hurdle only below ~$2,901, so quality does not rescue the price.
moat_for: Lot-option (LPA) model: finished lots controlled via fixed-price agreements, ~10% deposits — land risk and capital intensity structurally removed
Returns on capital far above peers through full cycles (ROE above 30%; FY2025 ~34.7%) on the small capital base
Build-to-order model with pre-sold backlog (10,998 units / $4.99B at Q2 2026) limits speculative inventory
Mortgage banking capture rate 85% (Q2 2026) — attached, capital-light ancillary earnings
Decades of disciplined buybacks: share count shrinking 4.4%/yr, $1.78B repurchased TTM per fundamentals.json
Leading share in Mid-Atlantic markets (Washington DC / Baltimore corridors)
moat_against: Peers (Lennar, D.R. Horton) are copying the asset-light lot-option model, narrowing the structural edge
No buyer switching costs or pricing power in a downturn: Q2 2026 gross margin 19.2% vs 21.5%, order ASP -5%, incentives rising
Lot supply depends on third-party developers — no owned land bank to fall back on if developers fail or reprice
Geographic concentration: 37 metro areas in 16 states + Washington DC, East-Coast heavy
Hostage to mortgage rates and affordability; earnings are cyclical even if the balance sheet is not
